title: Pout Kaomoji (｀ε´): Copy & Paste Sulky & Pouting Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste pout kaomoji: pouting faces like (｀ε´) and (￢з￢), puffed cheeks ٩(๑`^´๑)۶, grumpy (︶︹︺) and sulky (￣^￣) for when you are upset, not raging.
hero_tagline: Pursed lips, puffed cheeks and a grumpy hmph for being upset without flipping a table. Pick a pout and it copies straight away.
intro: A pout kaomoji pushes the lips forward. ε and з, a Greek and a Cyrillic letter, both look like pursed lips seen from the side, and the frowning brows ` and ´ around them make the face sulky. The same lips appear in kiss faces like (*^3^), so the brows decide the meaning: happy closed eyes plus 3 is a kiss, angled brows plus ε is a pout. ^ as a mouth reads as puffed cheeks. These faces are for being annoyed, hurt or grumpy. When the mood is shouting or rage, with 益 teeth and ╬ anger veins, use the angry kaomoji page linked below.

sections.label: Pouting Lips
sections.intro: The ε and з mouths. Angled brows make it a sulk; soft eyes make it a mild complaint.

sections.label: Puffed Cheeks
sections.intro: ^ as a mouth reads as cheeks full of air, the cartoon sign of a child refusing to talk.

sections.label: Hmph
sections.intro: The face for "fine, whatever". ￣^￣ points the nose up and away.

sections.label: Grumpy
sections.intro: ︶︹︺ is a downturned brow and mouth, the grumpiest frown in the set. Use these for a bad mood that has not boiled over.

faq.q: What does ε mean in a kaomoji?
faq.a: ε is the Greek letter epsilon, and side-on it looks like pursed, pushed-out lips. With frowning brows, as in (｀ε´), it is a pout; with happy eyes and a heart nearby, the same shape is a kiss.

faq.q: What is the difference between a pout kaomoji and an angry kaomoji?
faq.a: A pout is sulky or hurt and keeps the mouth closed: pursed lips, puffed cheeks, a hmph. Angry faces open the mouth to shout and add marks like 益 for bared teeth or ╬ for a throbbing vein.
For upset but not furious, (︶︹︺) and ( ˘︹˘ ) are frowning and withdrawn, and (◞‸◟) looks deflated. For upset and complaining, the pouting (｀ε´) says it more loudly.
